question: When did William Shakespeare die?
fact: Shakespeare died in Stratford-upon-Avon in April 1616. Miguel de Cervantes died the same week in Madrid.

question: When did the Titanic sink?
fact: The Titanic sank on 15 April 1912, on its maiden voyage, after hitting an iceberg in the North Atlantic.

question: When did humans first land on the Moon?
fact: Apollo 11 landed on 20 July 1969. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the surface while Michael Collins orbited above.

question: When did the Berlin Wall fall?
fact: The Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989, after standing for 28 years.

question: When did the First World War begin?
fact: Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia on 28 July 1914, a month after Archduke Franz Ferdinand was shot in Sarajevo.

question: When did the Second World War end?
fact: The war in Europe ended in May 1945, and Japan formally surrendered on 2 September 1945.

question: When did Christopher Columbus first reach the Americas?
fact: Columbus made landfall in the Bahamas on 12 October 1492, believing he had reached Asia.

question: When was the US Declaration of Independence adopted?
fact: The Continental Congress adopted the Declaration on 4 July 1776, which is why the US celebrates on the Fourth of July.

question: When was the Bastille stormed, starting the French Revolution?
fact: Crowds stormed the Bastille prison in Paris on 14 July 1789. France still celebrates the date as its national day.

question: When did the Wright brothers make the first powered aeroplane flight?
fact: Orville Wright flew for 12 seconds at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, on 17 December 1903.

question: When did Finland become independent?
fact: Finland declared independence from Russia on 6 December 1917, still celebrated as Independence Day.

question: When was the first iPhone released?
fact: Steve Jobs unveiled the iPhone in January 2007, and it went on sale in the US that June.

question: When was Napoleon defeated at the Battle of Waterloo?
fact: Napoleon lost at Waterloo, in present-day Belgium, on 18 June 1815, and was exiled to Saint Helena.

question: When did the Soviet Union break up?
fact: Mikhail Gorbachev resigned on 25 December 1991, and the Soviet Union was dissolved the next day.

question: When was Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, launched?
fact: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on 4 October 1957. Its simple radio beep could be heard around the world.

question: When did the Great Fire of London happen?
fact: The Great Fire started in a bakery on Pudding Lane in September 1666 and burned for about four days.

question: When did Martin Luther publish his 95 Theses?
fact: Luther's 95 Theses of 1517 are usually taken as the start of the Protestant Reformation.

question: When did the Black Death arrive in Europe?
fact: The plague reached Sicily in 1347 on ships from the Black Sea, and spread across Europe over the next few years.

question: When did Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart die?
fact: Mozart died in Vienna in December 1791, aged 35, leaving his Requiem unfinished.

question: When was the Eiffel Tower completed?
fact: The Eiffel Tower was finished in 1889 for the Paris World's Fair, a hundred years after the French Revolution.

question: When did Charles Darwin publish On the Origin of Species?
fact: On the Origin of Species came out in November 1859, and the first printing sold out quickly.

question: When did the Chernobyl nuclear disaster happen?
fact: Reactor 4 at Chernobyl, in Soviet Ukraine, exploded on 26 April 1986.

question: When was Nelson Mandela elected President of South Africa?
fact: Mandela became president after South Africa's first fully democratic election in April 1994.

question: When did the Wall Street Crash happen?
fact: The crash of October 1929 helped start the Great Depression of the 1930s.

question: When was the Battle of Hastings?
fact: William the Conqueror defeated King Harold II at Hastings in October 1066 and took the English throne.

question: When was Magna Carta sealed?
fact: King John sealed Magna Carta at Runnymede, near London, in June 1215.

question: In what year BC was Julius Caesar assassinated?
fact: Caesar was stabbed in Rome on the Ides of March, 15 March 44 BC.

question: When did Isaac Newton publish his Principia, with the laws of motion?
fact: Newton's Principia, published in 1687, set out his three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation.

question: When did Albert Einstein publish his theory of special relativity?
fact: 1905 is called Einstein's miracle year: he published four major papers, including special relativity and E = mc².

question: When did the first website go online?
fact: Tim Berners-Lee put the first website online at CERN in 1991. It explained what the World Wide Web was.

question: When did euro coins and notes go into circulation?
fact: Euro cash arrived on 1 January 2002. The euro had existed on paper since 1999.

question: When was the first FIFA World Cup played?
fact: Uruguay hosted and won the first World Cup in 1930.

question: When did Queen Elizabeth II die?
fact: Elizabeth II died in September 2022, after 70 years on the throne.

question: When did the Beatles release their first album, Please Please Me?
fact: Please Please Me came out in March 1963 and was recorded mostly in a single day.

question: When was Facebook launched?
fact: Facebook launched in February 2004, first only for Harvard students.

question: When was Google founded?
fact: Larry Page and Sergey Brin founded Google in September 1998.

question: When did Hurricane Katrina hit New Orleans?
fact: Hurricane Katrina struck the US Gulf Coast in August 2005.

question: When did the Panama Canal open?
fact: The Panama Canal opened in August 1914, just as the First World War began in Europe.

question: When was Nokia founded?
fact: Nokia started in 1865 as a pulp mill founded by Fredrik Idestam in Finland.

question: When did Finland join the European Union?
fact: Finland joined the EU on 1 January 1995, together with Sweden and Austria.

question: When did Finland join NATO?
fact: Finland became NATO's 31st member in April 2023.

question: When did Helsinki host the Summer Olympics?
fact: Helsinki hosted the Summer Olympics in 1952, after the 1940 Games it was due to host were cancelled.

question: When did the Sydney Opera House open?
fact: The Sydney Opera House opened in October 1973, years late and far over budget.

question: When did the Hindenburg airship disaster happen?
fact: The Hindenburg caught fire while landing in New Jersey in May 1937.

question: In what year was Pompeii buried by the eruption of Vesuvius?
fact: Mount Vesuvius erupted in AD 79 and buried Pompeii and Herculaneum.

question: When was the first Harry Potter book published?
fact: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone was published in the UK in June 1997.

question: When did Yuri Gagarin become the first person in space?
fact: Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth once in April 1961, in a flight that lasted about 108 minutes.

question: When did Mount St. Helens erupt?
fact: Mount St. Helens in Washington state erupted in May 1980, and its north face collapsed in a huge landslide.

question: When did the Spanish flu pandemic begin?
fact: The Spanish flu began in 1918 and spread around the world in several waves.

question: When was the Statue of Liberty dedicated?
fact: The Statue of Liberty, a gift from France, was dedicated in New York Harbor in October 1886.

question: When did the American Civil War end?
fact: The American Civil War ended in 1865, the same year Abraham Lincoln was assassinated.

question: When was the first email sent between two computers?
fact: Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email in 1971 and chose the @ sign for addresses.

question: When did the Brooklyn Bridge open?
fact: The Brooklyn Bridge opened in May 1883, then the longest suspension bridge in the world.

question: When did Princess Diana die?
fact: Princess Diana died in a car crash in Paris in August 1997.

question: When did Alexander Graham Bell patent the telephone?
fact: Alexander Graham Bell was granted his telephone patent in March 1876.

question: When did Charles Lindbergh fly solo across the Atlantic?
fact: Lindbergh flew nonstop from New York to Paris in May 1927, in about 33 and a half hours.

question: When did Alexander Fleming discover penicillin?
fact: Fleming noticed in 1928 that a mould had killed the bacteria around it in a lab dish.

question: When was the first Super Mario Bros. game released?
fact: Super Mario Bros. came out in Japan in September 1985 for the Nintendo Famicom.

question: When was Wikipedia launched?
fact: Wikipedia went online in January 2001.

question: When was YouTube launched?
fact: YouTube's first video, Me at the zoo, was uploaded in April 2005.

question: When did Finland's Winter War begin?
fact: The Soviet Union attacked Finland on 30 November 1939, starting the Winter War.

question: When was Tetris created?
fact: Alexey Pajitnov created Tetris in 1984 in Moscow.

question: When was the first Star Wars film released?
fact: Star Wars, later called A New Hope, opened in cinemas in May 1977.

question: When was Ludwig van Beethoven born?
fact: Beethoven was born in Bonn in December 1770.

question: When did Leonardo da Vinci die?
fact: Leonardo da Vinci died in France in May 1519.

question: When was the first Angry Birds game released?
fact: Finland's Rovio released Angry Birds for the iPhone in December 2009.

question: When did Linus Torvalds first release Linux?
fact: Linus Torvalds, a Finnish student in Helsinki, released the first Linux kernel in 1991.

question: When did the Moomins first appear in a book?
fact: Tove Jansson's first Moomin book, The Moomins and the Great Flood, came out in 1945.

question: When did the Golden Gate Bridge open?
fact: The Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco opened in May 1937.

question: When was the Hubble Space Telescope launched?
fact: The Space Shuttle Discovery carried Hubble into orbit in April 1990.

question: When was the Berlin Wall built?
fact: East Germany began building the Berlin Wall in August 1961.
